title: Beware of the Free On-site Trap! China Unicom's Anti-Telecom Fraud Model Accurately Identifies Fraudulent VOIP Black Boxes, Safeguarding People's Communication Security
excerpt: Recently, the field of China Telecom's network security has witnessed a classic case of technological empowerment in solving a criminal case. China Unicom Fushu
content_html:
Recently, the field of China Telecom's network security has witnessed a classic case of technological empowerment in solving a criminal case. China Unicom Fushun Branch, relying on the group's self-developed anti-fraud large model system, successfully identified and dismantled a deeply hidden illegal VOIP communication equipment site in collaboration with local public security authorities, and the suspect has been legally arrested.

The incident began in August this year, when China Unicom's anti-fraud large model system issued an emergency alert during routine monitoring, accurately identifying a suspicious telecom network fraud risk clue in a certain area. Upon receiving the system alert, Fushun Unicom responded quickly, arranging staff to conduct on-site verification under the guise of regular line inspections. After careful inspection, staff discovered a set of illegally installed fraud-related VOIP communication devices in a hidden location.

During the verification process, a suspicious person suddenly appeared and attempted to carry out abnormal behavior. The staff acted decisively, immediately called the police, and provided detailed information about the scene, the specific location of the equipment, and the suspect's physical characteristics to the local police station. Subsequently, the suspect was apprehended on the spot. According to preliminary police confirmation, the suspect is indeed suspected of telecom network fraud, and the relevant illegal facts have been basically ascertained.

VOIP devices are commonly referred to as "black boxes" in the black industry chain. These communication devices can convert and disguise fraud calls made from abroad into regular domestic phone numbers, and even use the "official attributes" of unit landline numbers to lower victims' vigilance, thereby significantly increasing the success rate of fraud.

It is worth noting that criminals have recently frequently changed their methods of operation, and cases have emerged in many places where fraud groups have used the names of "on-site broadband maintenance," "free network speed-up," or "reissue gifts" to gain trust and enter residents' homes or units, secretly installing VOIP devices. Especially for the elderly population who lack young people at home, they often lack awareness of prevention against those wearing uniforms or claiming to be professional technicians, making them easy targets for such traps.

In response, relevant operators and the police jointly remind the public: when facing various services that claim to install, maintain, or upgrade networks under the banner of free services, be highly vigilant, strictly verify the identity of the other party, and confirm the information through the official customer service channels of the operator. If you find an unknown communication "black box" appearing suddenly at home or in your unit, stop using it immediately and report to the public security authorities as soon as possible, working together to cut off the dark tentacles of telecom network fraud.
